analysis.subject: civics
analysis.pageCoverage: The page covers the constitutional basis for impeachment, the step-by-step roles of the House and Senate, the standards for charges and the historical record of impeachments and removals.

overview.headline: How Congress charges, tries and removes federal officials

keyPoints.point: Impeachment is the process of bringing charges against a person in office for wrongdoing before any trial.
keyPoints.quote: Impeachment is the process of bringing charges against a government official for wrongdoing.

keyPoints.point: A person holding federal office can be impeached for treason, bribery and other high crimes and misdemeanors.
keyPoints.quote: An official can be impeached for treason, bribery, and “other high crimes and misdemeanors.”

keyPoints.point: The Senate holds an impeachment trial and the chief justice presides when a president is tried.
keyPoints.quote: The Senate holds an impeachment trial.

keyPoints.point: The House has initiated impeachment proceedings more than 60 times but recorded only 21 impeachments.
keyPoints.quote: The House has initiated impeachment proceedings more than 60 times. But there have been only 21 impeachments.

keyTerms.gloss: Process of bringing charges against a person in office for wrongdoing
keyTerms.quote: Impeachment is the process of bringing charges against a government official for wrongdoing.

keyTerms.gloss: Formal charges the House brings to start an impeachment case
keyTerms.quote: The House of Representatives brings articles (charges) of impeachment against an official.

keyTerms.gloss: Betrayal of the country listed with bribery as grounds for impeachment that includes treason
keyTerms.quote: An official can be impeached for treason, bribery, and “other high crimes and misdemeanors.”

keyTerms.gloss: Chamber that holds the impeachment trial after the House vote
keyTerms.quote: The Senate holds an impeachment trial.

keyTerms.gloss: Senate decisions of not guilty that let presidents remain in office after trial
keyTerms.quote: Presidents Johnson, Clinton, and Trump remained in office following acquittals by the Senate on all charges.

componentPlan.pedagogicalReason: The page lists the impeachment process as numbered steps that students must order correctly.
componentPlan.focusQuote: The House of Representatives brings articles (charges) of impeachment against an official.

componentPlan.pedagogicalReason: Historical counts and outcomes provide checkable facts that reinforce the process with concrete examples.
componentPlan.focusQuote: Of those who were impeached, only eight officials were found guilty by the Senate and removed from office.
